title: Eight Children in a Three-Bedroom House: How Makini School Began
conflicts: Starting place: 'three-bedroom house' (Okelo, HBS 2015 and How we made it in Africa 2013) vs 'home backyard' (Business Daily 2011) vs 'colonial bungalow where the founders lived' (Business Today 2018); her own words used. 'First' claims: first African woman Barclays branch manager (Columbia, Paukwa) vs first woman bank manager in Kenya (Kenyans.co.ke); narrower claim used. Pupil numbers 400 (1989) and 1,600 (1997) only in the 2002 Columbia case, attributed to it; Business Daily 2011 says 'more than 1,000'. The 2018 sale left out: Business Today says Schole bought all the shares, Kenyans.co.ke says a 71 per cent stake for nearly Ksh1 billion.
notes: Co-founder Pius Okelo added to founder field. HBS transcript cited via its Wayback Machine copy (hbs.edu blocks). The two PDFs load but the checker cannot read names in them; five other sources are OK. Quote stance: affirms.
